content: 1. Administer sulfadiazine at a dose of 5 g orally four times daily, or 150 mg/kg/day divided every 4–6 hours orally, with a maximum daily dose of 4 g/m². Folinic acid (5 mg every third day) should be co-administered with pyrimethamine and folinic acid at 100 mg/kg/day divided every 6 hours orally for 12 months. This regimen is used for the prophylaxis of recurrent rheumatic fever. Renal function and complete blood count (CBC) should be monitored during treatment. 2. Aminobenzoate potassium reduces the efficacy of sulfadiazine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 3. Aminolevulinic acid (oral) and sulfadiazine may increase each other's toxicity via pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Additionally, avoid administering other phototoxic drugs with aminolevulinic acid (oral) during the perioperative period (24 hours). 4. Sulfadiazine increases the toxicity of aminolevulinic acid (topical) through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of photosensitizing drugs may enhance phototoxic reactions during photodynamic therapy with aminolevulinic acid. 5. Sulfadiazine increases the effects of antithrombin alfa and antithrombin III by decreasing their metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 6. Sulfadiazine increases the effects of argatroban by decreasing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 7. Sulfadiazine decreases the efficacy of live BCG vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 8. Sulfadiazine increases the effects of bemiparin, bivalirudin, dalteparin, enoxaparin, fondaparinux, and heparin by decreasing their metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 9. Sulfadiazine increases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. 10. Sulfadiazine decreases the efficacy of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may act against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 11. Sulfadiazine increases the effects of methotrexate by plasma protein binding competition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 12. Sulfadiazine and methyl aminolevulinate increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Both drugs may increase each other's photosensitizing effects. 13. Sulfadiazine decreases the efficacy of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 14. Sulfadiazine and pexidartinib both increase the risk of hepatotoxicity. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Pexidartinib is associated with hepatotoxicity; avoid combining it with other hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements. 15. Sulfadiazine increases the effects of phenindione by decreasing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 16. Sulfadiazine increases the effects of protamine by decreasing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 17. Sulfadiazine increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Caution is advised if siponimod is co-administered with moderate CYP2C9 inhibitors. 18. Sulfadiazine and tretinoin (oral or topical) increase each other's phototoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 19. Sulfadiazine decreases the efficacy of live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 20. Sulfadiazine decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens, estradiol, ethinyl estradiol, and other oral hormonal contraceptives by altering intestinal flora. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor patients. 21. Sulfadiazine increases the levels of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide by plasma protein binding competition and by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 22. Sulfadiazine increases the effects of various forms of insulin (e.g., insulin aspart, insulin detemir, insulin glargine) through unspecified mechanisms. Concomitant use may require insulin dosage adjustments and increased glucose monitoring. 23. Sulfadiazine increases the levels of lacosamide by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when co-administered with strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. 24. Sulfadiazine increases the levels or effects of lesinurad by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitor therapy closely and consider dose adjustments. 25. Sulfadiazine decreases the efficacy of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor patients. 26. Sulfadiazine increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting CYP2C9 activity. Consider reducing the dose of CYP2C9 substrates when co-administered with cannabidiol. 27. Sulfadiazine increases the levels of diclofenac by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Do not exceed a diclofenac dose of 50 mg twice daily. 28. Sulfadiazine increases the levels of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor patients. 29. Sulfadiazine increases the levels of dronabinol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 30. Sulfadiazine increases the levels of eluxadoline by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution when co-administering with strong CYP2C9/10 inhibitors. 31. Sulfadiazine decreases the levels of sulfadiazine when co-administered with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF due to CYP2C9 induction. Monitor therapy closely. 32. Sulfadiazine increases the levels of methoxsalen by pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to additive photosensitizing effects. Use caution and monitor patients.
